children: Shares of Ionic Digital fell 6.9% in the afternoon session after AI linked stocks continued to pull back as Anthropic slid nearly 14% following its debut, failing to revive confidence in the sector's spending boom.

Investors had looked to Anthropic's record $81.3 billion initial public offering and Nvidia's quarterly earnings beat under interim CEO Colette Kress to steady sentiment following Jensen Huang's resignation, CNBC reported. Instead, Anthropic's retreat toward its $83 offer price echoed Seaport Research warnings, covered by CNBC, that its valuation demands much faster revenue growth.

Separately, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook warned against delaying rate hikes ahead of an expected December increase. Compounding the concerns, President Donald Trump threatened penalties on overseas U.S. data-center builds as new Commerce Department export-licensing rules weighed on chipmakers.
After the initial drop, the shares shed some of the losses and rose to $55.11, down 5% from the previous close.
What is the market telling us

Ionic Digital’s shares are quite volatile and have had 16 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 1 day ago when the stock dropped 6.5% on the news that an early rally tied to Anthropic's debut faded amid AI financing doubts and hawkish Federal Reserve signals. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83, raising a record $81.3 billion and opening at $111.50 before paring gains near $96, CNBC reported. Rate pressure built after October Fed minutes showed almost all officials backed further hikes. A couple of officials saw room for a larger December move, amid concerns about rapid AI debt growth. Governor Christopher Waller floated a half-point December hike while non-voting St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned several increases may be needed before spring 2027, CNBC reported, keeping markets focused on inflation data. Higher rates squeeze AI stocks from both sides by reducing the present value of future cash flows and raising borrowing costs for data centers and compute capacity. Until outlays yield durable earnings, rate pressure can outweigh landmark AI debuts.

Ionic Digital is down 12.4% since the beginning of the year, and at $55.11 per share, it is trading 36.4% below its 52-week high of $86.64 from September 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Ionic Digital’s shares at the IPO in July 2026 would now be looking at an investment worth $876.12.
